name: Alma Pike
life: “I still remember a pupil reading aloud to an empty chair.” People around the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio know Alma by a small Sunday habit. Alma notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: The head said I wasn't ready for this book. I've read it to my pupils thirty-seven times.
appearance: Alma has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Look for short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a mustard canvas overshirt with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. In conversation Alma holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Alma talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Alma's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To read the difficult chapter to the former teacher.
family: Hollis Wick is Alma’s half-sibling. Alma calls about good news first. Hollis is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The upstairs lease*, Hollis says, “I want to swap homes with the upstairs family because my mother can't climb my stairs anymore.”
connections: Damian Neal. A child's declaration of love gives the teacher a difficult margin to read aloud.

reactions.situation: The former pupil offers to pay forty years of fines
reactions.response: Alma asks the library what it actually needs from the returning reader.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Alma says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
